issues.title: Game::ResetElapsedTime() does nothing under the default fixed time step
issues.summary: ResetElapsedTime sets its flag only when IsFixedTimeStep is false, while XNA 4.0 honours it in both modes, so a blocking load followed by ResetElapsedTime causes a catch-up burst of updates in CNA only.
issues.expected: XNA 4.0's Game.ResetElapsedTime (IL of Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Game) sets forceElapsedTimeToZero and resets the running-slowly counters unconditionally; Game.Tick tests that flag right after reading the clock, before the fixed/variable branch, and discards the frame's elapsed time. The standard XNA idiom - load a level synchronously inside Update, then call ResetElapsedTime() - therefore yields no catch-up updates.
issues.actual: In {{src:modules/runtime/src/Game.cpp|Game.cpp}}, ResetElapsedTime is if (!IsFixedTimeStep_) forceElapsedTimeToZero_ = true;, and Tick reads the flag only in its variable-step branch. Under the default fixed step the call is a no-op: after a 2-second load the accumulator is clamped to MaxElapsedTime (500 ms) and the next tick runs up to 29 back-to-back updates at the default 60 Hz before drawing (500 ms / 16.6667 ms, the last partial step carried over).

issues.title: GameTime.IsRunningSlowly follows FNA's lag counter, not XNA 4.0's rule
issues.summary: CNA sets IsRunningSlowly after five accumulated extra steps and clears it when the lag counter returns to zero; XNA 4.0 reports it when two multi-step ticks occur within 20 ticks and assigns it before each Update, so the flag differs tick by tick.
issues.expected: XNA 4.0's Game.Tick (IL) keeps updatesSinceRunningSlowly1/2: a tick that needs more than one step shifts counter 1 into counter 2 and zeroes counter 1; drawRunningSlowly = updatesSinceRunningSlowly2 < 20; and the value is written to GameTime.IsRunningSlowly before every Update of the tick.
issues.actual: CNA's fixed-step branch in {{src:modules/runtime/src/Game.cpp|Game.cpp}} uses FNA's updateFrameLag_: it adds stepCount - 1 per tick, sets the flag when the lag reaches 5, clears it only when the lag is back to 0, decrements the lag after single-step ticks, and assigns the flag after the tick's updates. A single two-step hitch never sets the flag in CNA; two hitches 15 ticks apart set it in XNA and not in CNA; and CNA's flag can stay set long after XNA's has cleared.

issues.title: Game::Dispose(true) walks Components by live index, so a component that removes itself or another during Dispose makes the loop skip one
issues.summary: XNA 4.0 copies the collection to an array before disposing; CNA re-reads the count and indexes the live collection, so a removal during a component's Dispose shifts later entries and the next component is never disposed by that pass.
issues.expected: XNA 4.0 (IL of Game.Dispose(bool)) copies Components into a new IGameComponent[] and disposes from the copy, which is needed because XNA's GameComponent.Dispose itself removes the component.

If a component's Dispose removes itself (the XNA behaviour a port may re-implement, see NEW-B10-15) or another component, every later entry shifts down one slot and the component that moved into slot i is skipped.

issues.title: Ray::Intersects(BoundingBox) and Ray::Intersects(BoundingSphere) differ from XNA 4.0 on degenerate and boundary rays
issues.summary: A zero-direction ray inside a box returns no hit (XNA: 0), axis parallelism uses a 2^-24 threshold where XNA uses 1e-6, and a ray starting exactly on a sphere and pointing outward returns no hit (XNA: 0, because XNA's inside test is <=).
issues.expected: XNA 4.0 (IL of BoundingBox.Intersects(ref Ray, out float?)): start with num = 0, treat an axis as parallel when Math.Abs(dir) < 1E-06, otherwise multiply by 1f / dir; a ray whose three axes are all parallel and whose origin is inside returns 0. Ray.Intersects(ref BoundingSphere, out float?) returns 0 when the squared centre distance is <= the squared radius.
issues.actual: {{src:modules/math/src/Ray.cpp|Ray.cpp}} uses FNA's slab algorithm: MathHelper::WithinEpsilon(dir, 0) (machine-epsilon threshold), division by the direction component, and an optional tMin that is never set when all three axes are parallel, so the zero-direction inside case returns std::nullopt. The sphere overload returns 0 only for differenceLengthSquared < sphereRadiusSquared; on the surface it falls through, and an outward direction gives a negative dot product and no hit.

issues.title: BoundingSphere::Contains(Vector3) and Contains(BoundingSphere) return different ContainmentType values from XNA 4.0
issues.summary: A point exactly on the surface is Intersects in CNA (XNA: Disjoint), and Contains(BoundingSphere) tests d^2 <= (R - r)^2, losing the sign of R - r, so a small sphere reports that it Contains a larger concentric sphere (XNA: Intersects).

The sphere overload's Contains test is sqDistance <= (Radius - sphere.Radius) * (Radius - sphere.Radius): squaring discards the sign, so a radius-1 sphere asked about a concentric radius-5 sphere answers Contains. BoundingSphere::Contains(BoundingBox) also builds on the point overload (corner != Disjoint), so a box touching the sphere at a corner is treated as inside.

issues.title: BoundingFrustum::Intersects differs from XNA 4.0: box and sphere overloads use a conservative plane test, and the Plane overload counts an on-plane corner as Intersecting
issues.summary: The box and sphere overloads report true for volumes just outside an edge or corner where XNA's exact GJK query reports false, and the Plane overload treats a zero corner distance as Intersecting (XNA: Back).
issues.expected: XNA 4.0 (IL): BoundingFrustum.Intersects(ref BoundingBox) and Intersects(ref BoundingSphere) run the Gjk helper, an exact convex-intersection query. Intersects(ref Plane) classifies each corner with dot + D > 0 as Front and everything else (including exactly 0) as Back.

The Plane overload uses Plane::IntersectsPoint, which returns Intersecting for a zero distance, so a frustum touching a plane from behind is Intersecting in CNA and Back in XNA.

issues.title: Vector, Matrix, Quaternion and CurveKey hash codes use raw float bits, so +0.0f and -0.0f components compare equal but hash differently
issues.summary: FloatHash returns the IEEE bit pattern, so Equals and GetHashCode disagree for values with a negative-zero component; .NET's Single.GetHashCode returns 0 for both zeros, keeping XNA's hashes consistent with Equals.
issues.public_contract: GetHashCode() of Vector2, Vector3, Vector4, Matrix, Quaternion and CurveKey
issues.expected: The Equals/GetHashCode contract: equal values have equal hashes. .NET Framework's Single.GetHashCode returns 0 when the value is 0, so XNA's component-sum hashes agree for +0 and -0.

issues.title: Color::FromNonPremultiplied(int r, int g, int b, int a) multiplies in 32-bit int, so large arguments overflow (undefined behaviour)
issues.summary: CNA computes r * a / 255 in int; XNA 4.0 widens to 64-bit long before multiplying and clamps the result, so arguments whose product exceeds INT_MAX are defined in XNA and undefined in CNA.

issues.expected: XNA 4.0 (IL): each channel is ClampToByte64((long)r * a / 255) - conv.i8 on both operands, a 64-bit multiply and divide, then a clamp.
issues.actual: {{src:modules/math/src/Color.cpp|Color.cpp}} computes static_cast<intcs>(r * a / ByteMax) with intcs operands. For in-range byte values this matches; for out-of-range inputs whose product exceeds INT_MAX (for example r = a = 50000) the multiplication overflows.

issues.title: BoundingSphere::CreateFromBoundingBox and the SmoothStep/Hermite/CatmullRom helpers use different arithmetic from XNA 4.0, and no oracle measures last-bit agreement
issues.summary: CreateFromBoundingBox and the SmoothStep/Hermite/CatmullRom helpers compute with formulas or precision that differ from XNA's, and only CreateFromPoints has an XNA oracle.

issues.title: GraphicsDeviceManager subscribes a lambda capturing this to GameWindow::ClientSizeChanged and never removes it
issues.summary: registerServices discards the subscription token and Dispose removes only the two services, so a manager destroyed or replaced while its game window lives leaves a dangling resize callback that the next resize invokes.

issues.actual: {{src:modules/runtime/src/GraphicsDeviceManager.cpp|GraphicsDeviceManager.cpp}}'s registerServices does game_->getWindowProperty().ClientSizeChanged += [this](...) { INTERNAL_OnClientSizeChanged(...); }; and keeps no token; unregisterServices (called from Dispose(bool)) removes only the IGraphicsDeviceManager and IGraphicsDeviceService entries. After the manager is destroyed, the next window resize calls INTERNAL_OnClientSizeChanged on freed memory.

issues.title: GraphicsDeviceManager::Dispose(bool) raises Disposed before setting disposed_, so a Disposed handler that disposes the manager again re-enters Dispose
issues.summary: The re-entrant guard is set after the event, so a handler that calls Dispose() on the manager (directly or through an owner's cleanup) re-runs the method and raises Disposed again, recursing until the handler stops.
issues.expected: Dispose must be idempotent, including when called from its own Disposed event; GraphicsDevice::Dispose(bool) in the same codebase sets its flag first for exactly this reason ("This makes reentrant Dispose idempotent").

A handler that calls Dispose() finds disposed_ still false, runs unregisterServices again and raises Disposed again.

issues.title: GraphicsDevice::Reset rolls back only the window and virtual-resolution stage; a later renderer failure leaves the new PresentationParameters stored and DeviceReset unraised
issues.summary: An exception from UpdatePresentationFormatEXT, ApplyMultiSampleCount or SetSwapInterval escapes after the new parameters are stored and render targets were unbound, and after DeviceResetting was raised, so the device reports settings it may not have applied.

issues.expected: CNA's own REMED-GFX-029 comment in the reset path states the intent: "a renderer resize is a failed Reset, not a partially successful one" - a failed reset restores the public presentation state before rethrowing.

issues.title: Sub-pixel SpriteBatch destinations reach only EasyGL, OPENGL4 and SOFTWARE; every other renderer truncates them to whole pixels
issues.summary: SpriteBatch forwards float destinations through ISpriteBatchRenderer's sub-pixel Draw overload, whose default truncates toward zero into an integer Rectangle; only the EasyGL, OPENGL4 and SOFTWARE sprite renderers override it.
issues.public_contract: SpriteBatch::Draw / DrawString with fractional positions or scales; ISpriteBatchRenderer::Draw(texture, float x, float y, float w, float h, ...)
issues.expected: XNA 4.0 carries sprite destinations as floats to the GPU, so a sprite at x = 10.5 lands between pixels and is filtered by the sampler (the interface comment in {{src:modules/graphics/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/Common/IGraphicsRenderer.hpp|IGraphicsRenderer.hpp}} says the same).
issues.actual: SpriteBatch calls the float overload for every queued sprite ({{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/SpriteBatch.cpp|SpriteBatch.cpp}}). The default implementation quantises each value with static_cast<int> (truncation toward zero, so -0.5 becomes 0) and forwards to the integer-Rectangle overload. Only EasyGLRenderer, OpenGL4SpriteBatchRenderer and the SOFTWARE sprite renderer override it; VULKAN, SDL_GPU, WEBGPU, the Direct3D renderers, DIRECT2D, GDI, SDL_RENDERER, the browser renderers, METAL, FNA3D and the rest draw on whole pixels. Smooth sub-pixel scrolling and fractional text scaling therefore snap on those renderers.

issues.summary: A texture rewritten between two Draw calls of an Immediate batch is rasterised with its final contents for every sprite; CNA documents this as a deliberate CNA-wide divergence (VULKAN-057).

issues.title: Disposing or destroying an untracked Texture2D/TextureCube copy raises GraphicsDevice.ResourceDestroyed although ResourceCreated was never raised for it
issues.summary: The GraphicsResource copy constructor neither registers the copy nor raises ResourceCreated, but Dispose(bool) (also run from the destructor) raises ResourceDestroyed for any live device, so every short-lived copy produces an unmatched destroy event.
issues.public_contract: GraphicsDevice::ResourceCreated / ResourceDestroyed events; GraphicsResource copy constructor and Dispose(bool)
issues.expected: ResourceCreated and ResourceDestroyed should pair up per resource, so tools that track live resources from the events stay balanced.
issues.actual: In {{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsResource.cpp|GraphicsResource.cpp}}, the device constructor calls AddResourceReference and OnResourceCreated; the copy constructor copies the device pointer, lifetime token, name and tag and does neither. Dispose(bool) calls OnResourceDestroyed(name_, tag_) and RemoveResourceReference whenever the device is alive, regardless of disposing, so destroying a copy raises a destroy event for a resource that was never announced. Copies are routine: ContentManager::Load<Texture2D> returns a copy on every cache hit.
issues.evidence: Checked by reading the named sources at 009d40f5; nothing was built or executed for this entry. Same root cause as CNA-BUG-029 (copies bypass device tracking), published by an earlier package; this entry records the event-pairing symptom that entry does not mention.
issues.reproduction:
// Illustrative; not compiled or run for this entry.
int created = 0, destroyed = 0;
device.ResourceCreated   += [&](auto*, auto&) { ++created; };
device.ResourceDestroyed += [&](auto*, auto&) { ++destroyed; };
Texture2D original(device, 4, 4);   // created = 1
{ Texture2D copy = original; }      // destroyed = 1 (copy's destructor)
original.Dispose();                // destroyed = 2, created still 1

issues.title: DIRECTX9 reports AnisotropicFiltering and MultiSampleAntiAliasing unconditionally and writes MaxAnisotropy to the sampler without clamping to the device cap
issues.summary: DirectX9Renderer inherits the interface's default true capability answers, and its fixed-function/stock ApplySamplerState passes the requested MaxAnisotropy straight to D3DSAMP_MAXANISOTROPY, although its compiled-effect path clamps to D3DCAPS9::MaxAnisotropy.
issues.expected: A capability answer should describe the device, and a sampler value should be clamped to what the device accepts, as the renderer's own compiled-effect route does.
issues.actual: {{src:modules/renderers/directx9/src/DirectX9Renderer.cpp|DirectX9Renderer.cpp}} has no SupportsCapability override, so the default in IGraphicsRenderer answers true for anisotropic filtering and MSAA on every device, while multisampling itself is decided later by CheckDeviceMultiSampleType in ClampMultiSampleCountEXT. ApplySamplerState sets D3DSAMP_MAXANISOTROPY to the requested value unchecked; {{src:modules/renderers/directx9/src/D3D9CompiledEffect.cpp|D3D9CompiledEffect.cpp}} clamps the same state to [1, caps.MaxAnisotropy].

issues.evidence: Checked by reading the named sources at 009d40f5; nothing was built or executed for this entry. Direct3D 9 drivers generally tolerate out-of-range anisotropy values, so the visible effect is driver-dependent; the capability answer is wrong only on devices without the feature.

issues.title: METAL refuses a large part of the graphics API until it has macOS evidence: MRT, custom effects, occlusion queries, instancing, multi-stream input, back-buffer readback and several sampler/blend states

issues.title: CANVAS and FREEDIRECT ignore GraphicsDevice.Viewport and ScissorRectangle, and SDL_RENDERER ignores Viewport
issues.summary: The renderers leave the no-op IGraphicsRenderer::SetViewport (and, on CANVAS and FREEDIRECT, SetScissorRect) in place, so a custom viewport never offsets drawing and a scissor rectangle never clips there.
issues.public_contract: GraphicsDevice.Viewport and GraphicsDevice.ScissorRectangle (with RasterizerState.ScissorTestEnable) on CANVAS, FREEDIRECT and SDL_RENDERER
issues.expected: XNA SpriteBatch and 3D drawing honour the device viewport, and an enabled scissor rectangle clips rasterisation - split-screen and UI clipping depend on both.
issues.actual: IGraphicsRenderer::SetViewport and SetScissorRect are empty defaults in {{src:modules/graphics/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/Common/IGraphicsRenderer.hpp|IGraphicsRenderer.hpp}}. CANVAS ({{src:modules/renderers/canvas/src/CanvasRenderer.cpp|CanvasRenderer.cpp}}) and FREEDIRECT ({{src:modules/renderers/freedirect/src/FreeDirectRenderer.cpp|FreeDirectRenderer.cpp}}) override neither, and SDL_RENDERER ({{src:modules/renderers/sdl-renderer/src/SdlRenderer.cpp|SdlRenderer.cpp}}) overrides only SetScissorRect. GraphicsDevice validates and stores the values, so the getters round-trip while nothing changes on screen. SDL_RENDERER also has no applied-format override, so PresentationParameters keeps the requested depth format (for example Depth24) on a renderer without a depth buffer. The SDL_RENDERER scissor-enable defect is published separately as NEW-B10-49.
issues.evidence: Checked by reading the named sources at 009d40f5; nothing was built or executed for this entry. Established by grepping the three renderers' headers and sources for the overrides.

issues.regression_test: Register the shared viewport and scissor fixtures for these renderers, or make them refuse the settings explicitly and test the refusal.
issues.blast_radius: Split-screen, letterboxed UI and clipped scroll panels on the three 2D renderers.

issues.title: SDL_RENDERER clips to any non-empty ScissorRectangle even when RasterizerState.ScissorTestEnable is false
issues.summary: SdlRenderer::SetScissorRect installs SDL_SetRenderClipRect for every non-empty rectangle and the renderer has no ApplyRasterizerState override, so a game that sets a scissor rectangle but draws with the test disabled is still clipped.
issues.public_contract: GraphicsDevice.ScissorRectangle together with RasterizerState.ScissorTestEnable on SDL_RENDERER
issues.expected: XNA clips only while RasterizerState.ScissorTestEnable is true; the rectangle may stay set while other draws run unclipped (a common UI pattern).
issues.actual: {{src:modules/renderers/sdl-renderer/src/SdlRenderer.cpp|SdlRenderer.cpp}}'s SetScissorRect calls SDL_SetRenderClipRect(renderer, &rect) for any rectangle with positive size and clears the clip only for an empty one; the scissor-enable flag arrives through ApplyRasterizerState, which SDL_RENDERER does not override (the interface default ignores it). So the clip follows the rectangle, not the test: disabled-test draws are clipped, and an enabled zero-area rectangle removes clipping entirely.
issues.evidence: Checked by reading the named sources at 009d40f5; nothing was built or executed for this entry.
issues.reproduction:
// Illustrative; not compiled or run for this entry.
device.setScissorRectangleProperty(Rectangle(0, 0, 100, 100));
batch.Begin(SpriteSortMode::Deferred, BlendState::AlphaBlend, nullptr, nullptr,
            RasterizerState::CullCounterClockwise);   // ScissorTestEnable = false
batch.Draw(background, Rectangle(0, 0, 800, 600), Color::White);
batch.End();
// XNA: full background.  SDL_RENDERER: only the 100x100 corner is drawn.
issues.tests_current: sdlrenderer_rasterizer_depthstencil_construction_test.cpp checks state construction only; no SDL_RENDERER pixel test toggles ScissorTestEnable.
issues.regression_test: A pixel fixture that sets a small ScissorRectangle and draws full-screen with the test disabled and then enabled, asserting unclipped and clipped results.
issues.blast_radius: UI and HUD code on SDL_RENDERER that leaves a scissor rectangle set between clipped and unclipped passes.
issues.workaround: Reset ScissorRectangle to the full viewport before unclipped draws.

Code can read or set them through Parameters[name].

issues.title: DIRECTX9 runs a ShaderEffect only inside SpriteBatch; a 3D draw with a ShaderEffect silently uses the stock-effect cascade while CustomEffects reports true
issues.summary: DIRECTX9 compiles and runs ShaderEffect HLSL for SpriteBatch, but its 3D draw dispatch has no custom-effect branch, and its capability answers describe neither route correctly.
issues.public_contract: ShaderEffect (CNA extension) with GraphicsDevice::DrawPrimitives/DrawIndexedPrimitives on DIRECTX9; GraphicsCapability::CustomEffects; RendererCapabilityProfile
issues.expected: A renderer that reports CustomEffects must either run the custom program for every draw route or refuse the ones it cannot run; CNA's DIRECTX11/12 declare ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT() = true and an HLSL dialect.
issues.actual: {{src:modules/renderers/directx9/src/DirectX9Renderer.cpp|DirectX9Renderer.cpp}}'s CreateEffectRenderer compiles the caller's HLSL (SM2/SM3) into a D3D9EffectRenderer, and {{src:modules/renderers/directx9/src/D3D9SpriteBatch.cpp|D3D9SpriteBatch.cpp}} uses it for SpriteBatch. {{src:modules/renderers/directx9/src/D3D9EffectDraw.cpp|D3D9EffectDraw.cpp}}'s DrawPrimitivesExImpl dispatches compiled effects, PBR and the five stock effects and never reads the custom-effect renderer, so a 3D draw bound to a ShaderEffect is drawn with a stock shader instead. Because DirectX9Renderer overrides neither SupportsCapability, GetShaderDialectEXT nor ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT, the device reports CustomEffects supported and the capability profile says ShaderEffect source never determines pixels - wrong for SpriteBatch, and the 3D route gives no refusal.
issues.evidence: Checked by reading the named sources at 009d40f5; nothing was built or executed for this entry. XNA games use compiled effects, which DIRECTX9 supports separately; ShaderEffect is a CNA extension.
issues.tests_current: DIRECTX9 ShaderEffect tests cover SpriteBatch; none draws 3D geometry with a ShaderEffect.

issues.title: The renderer capability profile reports every ShaderDialect* feature Unsupported on SDL_GPU (and VULKAN) because their declared dialect, SpirV, has no feature entry
issues.summary: BuildRendererCapabilityProfileEXT maps a renderer's GetShaderDialectEXT onto six ShaderDialect* features; SpirV matches none, so SDL_GPU - which executes ShaderEffect source and, with libshaderc, compiles Vulkan-rule GLSL - appears to accept no dialect at all.
issues.expected: The capability profile exists so that a caller can choose shader source without trying it; a renderer that executes caller shaders should report at least one usable dialect (SupportsShaderLanguageEXT answers per stage).
issues.actual: BuildRendererCapabilityProfileEXT in {{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp|GraphicsDevice.cpp}} sets ShaderDialectGlslDesktop/GlslEs/GlslVulkan/Hlsl/Msl/Wgsl to supported only when ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT() is true and the declared dialect equals that enumerator. SDL_GPU ({{src:modules/renderers/sdl-gpu/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/SdlGpu/SdlGpuRenderer.hpp|SdlGpuRenderer.hpp}}) and VULKAN declare ShaderDialectEXT::SpirV, for which no feature exists, so all six read Unsupported. SDL_GPU with CNA_SDL_GPU_SHADER_EFFECTS compiles GLSL through libshaderc (the GlslVulkan dialect), which the profile therefore hides. (VULKAN additionally reports ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT false by design, because it consumes SPIR-V words rather than the engine layer's GLSL.)

issues.title: Stock-effect state is captured at draw time, so a property changed after EffectPass::Apply() affects the next draw, unlike XNA

The sequence effect.World = A; pass.Apply(); effect.World = B; Draw(); draws with B in CNA and with A in XNA.

issues.title: GameWindow keeps a raw pointer to the platform window owned by the Game's GraphicsDevice, and nothing clears it when the game disposes that device
issues.summary: Game's constructor hands GraphicsDevice_.GetPlatformWindowInternal() to Window_.setWindowInternal; GraphicsDevice::Dispose destroys the platform window (destroyNativeResources resets platformWindow_), after which GameWindow members dereference freed memory.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::GameWindow members after an explicit GraphicsDevice::Dispose() on the Game's device
issues.expected: A borrowed pointer must not outlive its owner; either GameWindow should be detached when the device destroys its window, or the device must not destroy a window the Game still exposes.
issues.actual: In {{src:modules/runtime/src/Game.cpp|Game.cpp}} the constructor calls Window_.setWindowInternal(GraphicsDevice_.GetPlatformWindowInternal(), ...). {{src:modules/runtime/src/GameWindow.cpp|GameWindow.cpp}} stores it in window_ and uses it for Title, AllowUserResizing, IsBorderless, ClientBounds, Handle and the rest. {{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp|GraphicsDevice.cpp}}'s destroyNativeResources (called by Dispose) resets the owning std::unique_ptr<IPlatformWindow>. Nothing rebinds or clears GameWindow::window_, so after a game disposes its device (the manager comments note "A game may explicitly dispose its device from Draw()") the next Window property call touches freed memory.

issues.title: Several live GraphicsDevices share process-wide window and input slots with last-writer semantics
issues.summary: The window-to-renderer registry is a static, unsynchronised map with no ownership check, and TextInputEXT and Mouse keep one process-wide window slot, so two devices overwrite each other's registry entries and input target.
issues.public_contract: IGraphicsRenderer::RegisterForWindow/UnregisterForWindow/GetForWindow; TextInputEXT and Mouse window binding with more than one GraphicsDevice
issues.expected: CNA allows several devices and caller-provided (borrowed) windows; each device's input routing and window lookup should stay correct while the others live.
issues.actual: RegisterForWindow in {{src:modules/graphics/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/Common/IGraphicsRenderer.hpp|IGraphicsRenderer.hpp}} does windowRegistry()[window] = renderer and UnregisterForWindow erases by window id, with no owner check and no lock; two devices attached to one borrowed window overwrite each other, and destroying either removes the survivor's entry (used by Mouse and the input bridge). {{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp|GraphicsDevice.cpp}}'s createOrAttachWindow sets the process-wide TextInputEXT and Mouse window slots to its window, and destroyNativeResources clears them only if they still point at it, so the last device created owns input. XNA's own Mouse.WindowHandle is also a single static slot.
issues.evidence: Checked by reading the named sources at 009d40f5; nothing was built or executed for this entry.
issues.tests_current: {{src:modules/graphics/tests/CNA/Internal/Renderers/Common/IGraphicsRendererWindowRegistryTests.cpp|IGraphicsRendererWindowRegistryTests.cpp}} pins distinct windows and replacement; SDL_GPU's constructor-exception test covers unregistration after a failed construction. Nothing covers two devices on one window, concurrent lookup, or two devices' input slots.
issues.regression_test: A test with two devices on one borrowed window (destroy one, the other stays registered) and a test of input routing with two live devices.
issues.blast_radius: Tools and editors that host several devices or share one window between devices; single-device games are unaffected.
issues.workaround: Use one GraphicsDevice per window and create input-owning devices last.

issues.title: A VULKAN occlusion query counts only the first contiguous run of its tagged draws per frame
issues.summary: Draws inside one Begin/End span that are separated by another query's draws or land in a later render pass after a boundary are not summed, by an approved 'reject additional spans' policy.
issues.expected: XNA counts every sample drawn between OcclusionQuery.Begin and End.
issues.actual: In {{src:modules/renderers/vulkan/src/VulkanRenderer.cpp|VulkanRenderer.cpp}} the record pass wraps each contiguous run of draws sharing a query tag in vkCmdBeginQuery/vkCmdEndQuery; a query already recorded this frame is "deliberately NOT reopened" because Vulkan requires a reset between begins ("this implements the approved 'reject additional spans beyond the first contiguous run' policy"). Later spans of the same query contribute nothing to PixelCount.
issues.evidence: Checked by reading the named sources at 009d40f5; nothing was built or executed for this entry.
issues.tests_current: Vulkan occlusion fixtures check single contiguous spans.
issues.regression_test: A fixture whose query spans a render-target switch (or an interleaved second query) and asserts the summed count, or documents the refusal.
issues.blast_radius: Occlusion queries whose draws are interleaved with other queries or split by render-pass boundaries on VULKAN.
issues.workaround: Keep each query's draws contiguous and inside one render pass.

issues.title: On VULKAN SpriteBatch draws between OcclusionQuery.Begin and End do not contribute to PixelCount
issues.summary: Only 3D draws are tagged with the active query (PushPending3DDraw is the only tagging site), so sprites drawn inside a query span are never counted and a sprite-only query reports 0.
issues.expected: XNA's occlusion query counts every sample written between Begin and End, whatever issued the draw; SpriteBatch-drawn visibility probes (for example a flare occlusion test) rely on it. Vulkan's own documentation in CNA lists occlusion queries as supported without this restriction.

issues.title: An enabled zero-area ScissorRectangle draws unclipped on VULKAN and SDL_GPU, while WEBGPU clips everything and METAL suppresses the draw
issues.summary: Vulkan's computeScissor and SDL_GPU's ApplyScissorForRef treat a zero width or height like a disabled scissor and use the full target; XNA's contract (rasterise only inside the rectangle) means nothing is drawn.
issues.public_contract: GraphicsDevice.ScissorRectangle with zero width or height and RasterizerState.ScissorTestEnable = true
issues.expected: With the scissor test enabled, only pixels inside the rectangle are written; an empty rectangle writes nothing (Direct3D 9, which XNA runs on, and WEBGPU and METAL in CNA behave this way).
issues.actual: {{src:modules/renderers/vulkan/src/VulkanRenderer.cpp|VulkanRenderer.cpp}}'s computeScissor returns the full framebuffer when !enabled || sw == 0 || sh == 0; {{src:modules/renderers/sdl-gpu/src/SdlGpuRenderer.cpp|SdlGpuRenderer.cpp}}'s ApplyScissorForRef takes its full-target branch unless scissorEnabled && scissorW > 0 && scissorH > 0. {{src:modules/renderers/webgpu/src/WebGPURenderer.cpp|WebGPURenderer.cpp}}'s ApplyDrawScissor clips an enabled empty rectangle to nothing. So a UI panel whose clip rectangle collapses to zero height draws its whole content over the screen on two renderers and disappears on the others.

batch.Draw(panelContent, Rectangle(0, 0, 800, 600), Color::White);
batch.End();
// Expected: nothing drawn. VULKAN / SDL_GPU: full-screen panel content.

issues.title: DIRECTX9 requests D3DPRESENT_INTERVAL_TWO without checking device support, and a failing Reset is then retried on every Present
issues.summary: PresentInterval::Two becomes D3DPRESENT_INTERVAL_TWO without a caps or windowed-mode check, and when Reset rejects it the renderer releases its default-pool resources and retries on every Present while still reporting Two.
issues.expected: An unsupported interval should be clamped (and the applied value reported) or refused once.
issues.actual: {{src:modules/renderers/directx9/src/DirectX9Renderer.cpp|DirectX9Renderer.cpp}}'s BuildPresentParameters switches on the interval with no caps check; SetSwapInterval marks the presentation dirty; EnsureDeviceSize (run from every Present) releases every D3DPOOL_DEFAULT resource, calls device_->Reset, and on failure keeps the previous size, sets presentationDirty_ = true and logs "retrying next frame". Direct3D 9 documents only DEFAULT, IMMEDIATE and ONE as valid for windowed swap chains, so a windowed game that asks for Two can enter this loop: a warning per frame and default-pool resources released and recreated every frame, with PresentationParameters still claiming Two.
issues.evidence: Checked by reading the named sources at 009d40f5; nothing was built or executed for this entry. The windowed-mode restriction is Direct3D 9's documented behaviour, not re-checked on a device; whether Wine/DXVK reject it the same way was not observed.
issues.tests_current: No DIRECTX9 test requests PresentInterval::Two.
issues.regression_test: A DIRECTX9 test that requests Two in a window and asserts that Reset succeeds once (clamped to One, applied value written back) or fails once with a clear exception.
issues.blast_radius: DIRECTX9 games that use PresentInterval::Two, especially windowed.
issues.workaround: Use PresentInterval::One with a fixed time step for 30 Hz pacing.

issues.summary: SetRenderTargets binds each MSAA target's multisample surface but does not track an MRT set, so when the set is unbound no StretchRect resolve runs and the textures keep stale contents.

issues.title: On DIRECTX9 a Texture2D can only be created with SurfaceFormat::Color
issues.summary: DIRECTX9 leaves ClassifySurfaceFormatEXT at its Defer default, so Texture2D creation falls back to a Color-only check although the renderer maps D3D formats internally; XNB textures still load because the reader converts them to RGBA.

The XNB Texture2D reader converts compressed data to RGBA when the renderer does not keep it compressed, so content loading is unaffected; programmatic creation is.

issues.title: SDL_Renderer_ClearOptions_Audit encodes Clear semantics that no longer exist and catches the wrong exception type, so it cannot pass at this snapshot
issues.summary: Clear now throws System::InvalidOperationException for any missing depth or stencil aspect, but the test expects Stencil-only clears not to throw and catches only std::runtime_error, which that exception does not derive from.
issues.expected: A registered test's expectations should match the current contract. {{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp|GraphicsDevice.cpp}}'s Clear(ClearOptions, ...) computes the available aspects (GetDefaultClearOptions, from HasRealBackBufferDepthBuffer/StencilBuffer) and throws System::InvalidOperationException ("Cannot clear depth or stencil because the device does not have an active depth or stencil buffer") for a requested aspect that is missing, as XNA does.
